notes: Wheels are an effective choice for warehouse robots operating on smooth, controlled floors. notes: A braided pneumatic actuator expands radially and shortens when pressurized. Its low actuator mass, large tensile force, and compliance make it useful for muscle-like attachment arrangements. The Puppy photograph is an example of pneumatic actuation in a biomimetic robot, not an energy-efficiency experiment. Air supply and control hardware must be included in any system-level efficiency claim. Source: submitted dissertation background and Bolen, Movement and Control of Biomimetic Humanoid Robots, slide 9. text: Dissertation Ch. 1, research motivation and objectives 9 Biology guides robot design; robot experiments test movement hypotheses Biological evidence Biomimetic robot Mechanics and neural principles Robot experiments generate biological predictions Goal: Better autonomous movement on unstructured terrain
notes: The first goal is to use biological principles to improve robots for unstructured environments. The reciprocal goal is to use increasingly biomimetic robots for controlled interventions that would be difficult or impossible in humans. For example, alter one actuator property or sensory pathway, measure the resulting movement, and generate a biological prediction to test. The return arrow represents a research process; this dissertation does not claim a new human experiment. Transition: the same understanding can inform devices that assist people.

text: Main-talk research questions 11 Three gaps limit prediction and testing of a biomimetic biped Force across lengths, pressures, and contraction Joint torque with compliance and bending Tests of coupled neural and body models
